extra_holder_sources.note: Vermont Elections Database, August 11, 2026 Democratic primary, Probate Judge, Addison County: Pam Marsh, 5,222 votes, unopposed -- the incumbent judge seeking re-election.
Vermont Judiciary, Probate Division Oversight Committee: lists Honorable Pamela Marsh as a Probate Judge member.

Vermont Elections Database, August 11, 2026 Democratic primary, Probate Judge, Bennington County: Lon T. McClintock, 1,946 votes, defeated Jim Dingley (1,765) -- the incumbent judge seeking re-election.

Vermont Judiciary, Advisory Committee on Rules of Probate Procedure, minutes of February 5, 2026: 'Hon. Annette Lorraine, the Caledonia Probate Judge, has been recommended to join the committee' -- she holds the seat in 2026.
Vermont Judiciary, Advisory Committee on Rules of Probate Procedure: lists Honorable Annette Lorraine as a Probate Judge member.
Vermont Elections Database, August 11, 2026 Democratic primary, Probate Judge, Chittenden County: Gregory J. Glennon, 22,830 votes, unopposed -- the incumbent judge seeking re-election.

Vermont Elections Database, August 11, 2026 Republican primary, Probate Judge, Franklin County: Bob Farrar, 1,782 votes, unopposed -- the incumbent judge seeking re-election (he also won the Democratic primary as a write-in).
Vermont Elections Database, August 11, 2026 Republican primary, Probate Judge, Grand Isle County: George 'Ned' Spear, 416 votes, unopposed -- the incumbent judge seeking re-election.

lamoille.note_extra: The court's own published notices style the judge 'James R. Dean Mahoney'; the ballot form printed in the official returns and the Elections Database is used here.

extra_holder_sources.note: Vermont Assistant Judges Association, Lamoille County courthouse page: lists 'PROBATE JUDGE Hon. James R. Dean Mahoney' among the county officials.
Vermont Superior Court, Probate Division, Lamoille Unit, published legal notice (September 25, 2024): signed 'Probate Judge, James R Dean Mahoney'.

orange.note_extra: The Elections Database and the official returns print the winner's name 'Kathryn c. A. Kennedy'; the Vermont Judiciary styles her 'Kathryn A.C. Kennedy'. The ballot form is used here.
